extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners evaluating/ prosecuting pre‑AIA patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining effective filing dates and for deciding and formulating rejections under the pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 provisions (102(a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g)), including when to apply each paragraph, applicable date rules, and required form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing date of a claimed invention (pre‑AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective filing date is the actual filing date of the U.S. application unless one of the exceptions (A),(B),(C) applies: (A) continuation/divisional with proper 35 U.S.C. 120/365(c) benefit — effective date is earliest filing date in chain; (B) continuation‑in‑part (CIP) — claims not supported by parent have effective date equal to new application filing date, while claims fully supported by earlier parent have parent's effective filing date; (C) proper claim of benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a provisional — effective date is the provisional filing date for claims fully supported by the provisional under 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual international filing date is the U.S. filing date for applications that entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. The foreign priority document filing date is not the claim’s effective filing date for pre‑AIA 102 purposes, although foreign priority dates may be used to overcome certain references. See MPEP §§ 1893.03(b), 211.01(c), 1895, 1895.01, 1896 for related rules. For CIPs, carefully determine which claims are fully supported by the earlier parent application and which are new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) when reference date is >1 year before effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference’s publication or issue date, or a public use or sale, is more than one year prior to the effective filing date of the claimed invention, it qualifies as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b), creating a statutory bar to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications, patents, public uses and sales that occur more than one year before the effective filing date should be rejected under 102(b) (statutory bar) rather than 102(a). If the one‑year grace period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday and the U.S. filing date is the next succeeding business day, the bar does not apply because of 35 U.S.C. 21(b). See MPEP §§ 2139.01 and 2133.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish public knowledge from public use/sale when choosing 102(a) vs 102(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere public knowledge of the invention does not warrant a 102(b) rejection (statutory bar), although it may support a rejection under 102(a). Evidence of public use or sale activity more than one year prior requires rejection under 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence points only to knowledge within the year prior to effective filing, apply 102(a). Do not make a 102(a) rejection where evidence shows the applicant made the invention and only disclosed it to others within the one‑year window (applicant's own disclosure may be protected by the grace period). See MPEP §§ 2132, 2133.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) when 102(b) is inapplicable and conditions met
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑AIA 102(e) permits using certain U.S. patent application publications, certain international application publications, and certain U.S. patents as of their U.S. filing dates (or certain international filing dates) as prior art when the reference was filed earlier than the applicant's invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior art date under 102(e) for an international application may be the international filing date only if (1) the international filing date is on or after November 29, 2000, (2) the international application designated the United States, and (3) the international application was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in the English language. Otherwise, the reference is available only under 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date. See MPEP § 2136 for detailed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive‑entity requirement for applying 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference may be applied under pre‑AIA 102(e) only if the inventive entity of the reference is different from that of the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are joint inventors, only one joint inventor needs to be different for inventive entities to be considered different; thus, 102(e) can apply even if some joint inventors are in common. If inventive entities are the same (or derivation/ownership issues apply), 102(e) may be disqualified. See MPEP § 2136.04 and related subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIPA (pre‑Nov‑29‑2000) 102(e) special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For references based on international applications filed prior to November 29, 2000, the 'pre‑AIPA' version of 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (as in force on November 28, 2000) applies. Patents issued from such international applications may only be used as prior art under the pre‑AIPA 102(e) date rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pre‑AIPA 102(e) date of such a prior art patent is the earliest of the date of compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2),(4), or the filing date of a later‑filed U.S. continuing application that properly claims benefit. Publications of international applications filed before Nov 29, 2000 do not have pre‑AIPA 102(e) dates at all, but may be prior art under 102(a) or 102(b) as of their publication dates. See subsection III and MPEP § 2136.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider pre‑AIA 102(a) even when 102(e) applies
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should still consider pre‑AIA 102(a) for a reference even if it is prior art under 102(e), because (1) the publication of an international application under PCT Article 21(2) may be the earliest prior art date under 102(a), and (2) 102(e) references used in an obviousness rejection under 103(a) may be disqualified under 103(c) if commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 102(a) to apply, the reference must have a publication date earlier than the application's effective filing date and must not be the inventor's or at least one joint inventor's own work. If an activity (sale/manufacture/disclosure) was by another entity, both 102(a) and 102(b) may be applicable depending on timing and evidence. See MPEP § 2139.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional/CIP/benefit claim rules for prior‑art dating
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is a continuation or divisional and meets 35 U.S.C. 120/365(c) requirements, claimed subject matter gets the earliest filing date in the chain. For CIPs, claims not supported by the parent get the new application's actual filing date; claims fully supported by the earlier parent get the parent's effective filing date. Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to provisionals may give provisional dates for supported claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining whether a reference is prior art, examiners must determine whether the subject matter relied upon is supported in the earlier application(s). Do not treat foreign priority dates as the effective filing date for pre‑AIA 102 purposes (though they may be used in other contexts). See MPEP § 2139.01 and related sections (1893.03(c), 211.01(c), 1895).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional benefit and support requirement under 35 U.S.C. 119(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference or claim is entitled to the benefit of a provisional application's filing date only if at least one of the claims in the reference is supported by the provisional application's written description in compliance with pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (now 112(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law (Dynamic Drinkware; Amgen v. Sanofi) requires that the provisional provide adequate written description support for the claim relied upon. Examiners must assess compliance with the written description requirement when attributing provisional dates to references. See MPEP ¶ 7.12.fti Examiner Note 2 and cited cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and required usage/order when making pre‑AIA 102 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the specified MPEP form paragraphs (¶ 7.06, ¶ 7.07.fti, ¶ 7.08.fti–¶ 7.15.fti, etc.) when issuing rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102; particular paragraphs must precede others and some are to be used only once per Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ¶ 7.06 (Notice re prior art available under both pre‑AIA and AIA) must be used in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on/after Mar 16, 2013 that claims priority to an earlier filing; ¶ 7.07.fti (Statement of Statutory Basis) is quoted in first actions on the merits and final rejections and is to be used only once in an Office action; ¶ 7.08.fti–¶ 7.14.fti correspond to the specific 102(a)–(g) paragraphs and must be preceded by ¶ 7.07.fti as indicated. Follow the Examiner Notes on when and how each form paragraph may/must be used and their required sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using provisional (provisional rejection) language for copending references under 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a copending application would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e) if published or patented, examiners may use provisional rejection form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.15.01.fti) to indicate a provisional rejection based on the copending application and identify the common relationship (common assignee/applicant/at least one common joint inventor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisional rejection must identify the copending application number, state the common relationship, and explain that the copending application would be prior art if published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) or patented. Ensure proper follow‑up paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.07.fti) and that necessary references and rationales are the same if adjusting statutory basis between AIA and pre‑AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business‑day filing rule for grace period calculations (35 U.S.C. 21(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the one‑year grace period would otherwise end on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, and the applicant's U.S. filing date is the next succeeding business day, the prior disclosure/public use/sale will not bar patenting under 102(b) due to 35 U.S.C. 21(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this rule when computing whether a printed publication, patent, public use, or sale occurred more than one year prior to the effective filing date; consult MPEP § 2139.02 and cited Ex parte Olah precedent for application.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to apply 102(a) because reference is the inventor’s own work or when disqualification under 103(c) applies
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference that is the inventor's own work (or that of at least one joint inventor) should not be applied as prior art under 102(a) as against that inventor; similarly, a reference used under 102(e)/(f)/(g) in a 103 rejection may be disqualified under pre‑AIA 103(c) if the reference and application were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a reference has an earlier filing/publication date, assess inventive authorship and ownership/assignment status before applying it against the applicant. Where disqualification applies, consider using 102(a) based on publication date where appropriate or refrain from applying the reference. See MPEP § 2139.02 and related sections concerning 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory paragraph‑specific form paragraph mapping and prerequisites (¶ 7.08.fti–¶ 7.14.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are distinct form paragraphs for each pre‑AIA 102 paragraph: ¶ 7.08.fti for 102(a), ¶ 7.09.fti for 102(b), ¶ 7.10.fti for 102(c), ¶ 7.11.fti for 102(d), ¶ 7.12.fti for 102(e) (with detailed Examiner Notes), ¶ 7.13.fti for 102(f), ¶ 7.14.fti for 102(g). Each must be used in the correct context and with required precedents (e.g., ¶ 7.07.fti).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Examiner Notes under each form paragraph for when it must be preceded by ¶ 7.07.fti, when it may be preceded by ¶ 7.08.fti/¶ 7.09.fti/etc., and special sub‑rules within ¶ 7.12.fti concerning PCT/publication/language/benefit claims. Use the exact statutory quotation where required in first actions on the merits and final rejections, and do not repeat once‑only paragraphs multiple times in an Office action.
